- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after sentiment turns negative; adjust downward by 1–2% for the first 5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model tends to overshoot and overcorrect; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% in the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (avg < -0.5), model underestimates true downside; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model often fails to capture the rebound; increase forecast by 0.3–0.8% in the first 3 days of the new sentiment phase.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to sentiment shifts; if sentiment changes direction within 3 days, adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid assuming linear continuation; if recent 7-day average is trending down, cap forecast at 1–2% below the 7-day low.
